name: Haze (one air for the whole world)
what: Replaces three.js's fog shader code once so every material fades into the same sun-tinted, luminous haze: a low patchy mist that lies in valleys, a thin haze everywhere and a deep layer for aerial perspective from high up, all tunable live through one shared uniform. Comes with a sky that melts into the same haze at the horizon, a warm key + cool fill light rig, drifting cloud shadows, reflections from the sky, and a measured final grade (Khronos Neutral tone map, contrast, saturation, sharpen, vignette, grain, faint bloom, sun shafts, an edge streak for speed).
use_when: an outdoor three.js world should feel big and atmospheric (valleys, coasts, cities, flying or open-world games), with far things fading into the sky instead of a hard fog wall or clear air.

third_party.what: three.js tone mapping functions and post-processing addons (UnrealBloomPass render body adapted)
third_party.author: three.js authors

good_for: Outdoor scenes with real depth: flying, gliding, open worlds, coasts, cities, mountain valleys, dawn or dusk moods. Works with every built-in material, instancing, skinning and MSAA; the haze itself works with the starter's renderer as is. Live tuning (one number for thickness).
not_for: Indoor or tiny scenes (little distance to fade), WebGPURenderer games, games that need clouds in the sky without a panorama (the procedural sky is a cloudless gradient), or stylised looks that draw their own fog.
